Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verses 1–7:

﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾: it is the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Musa (peace be upon him). It was said: al-Tur means every mountain, so He swore by the category of mountains. ﴿And by a Book inscribed﴾: it was said that this is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and it was said that it is the Qur'an, and it was said that it is the records of deeds. ﴿On parchment unrolled﴾: al-raqq (parchment) in the language means a page, but by custom it has been restricted to what is made of skin. And al-manshur (unrolled) is the opposite of folded. ﴿And by the House frequented﴾: it is a house in the seventh heaven, which every day seventy thousand angels enter, and they never return to it, and by this it is frequented. It is directly opposite the Ka'bah. It was said: al-Bayt al-Ma'mur is the Ka'bah and its being frequented by the pilgrims and those who circumambulate it. The first view is more apparent, and it is the statement of Ali and Ibn Abbas. ﴿And by the raised canopy﴾: this means the sky. ﴿And by the sea filled with fire (al-masjur)﴾: it is the sea of this world. It was said: it is a sea in the sky beneath the Throne. The first view is more apparent and more well known. The meaning of al-masjur is filled with water; it was said: it is empty of water. It is narrated that the seas' water will depart on the Day of Resurrection. The language allows both meanings, because the word is one of the antonyms (al-adhdad, words that carry opposite meanings). It was also said: its meaning is kindled with fire, from your saying "I heated the oven (sajartu al-tannur)." The language also supports this. It is narrated that Hell is in the sea. ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is certainly going to occur﴾: this is the answer to the oath, and it means the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 9:

﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently to and fro﴾. That is: it will move, going and coming. It was also said: it will revolve. And it was said: it will split apart. The element governing the adverbial phrase (al-'amil fi al-zarf) is either "waqi'" (will occur) and "dafi'" (will repel), or it is omitted.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verses 12–13:

﴿Those who are in vain discourse, playing.﴾ Al-khawd (immersion, plunging): floundering in falsehoods, likened to wading through water. ﴿The day they will be pushed violently into the fire.﴾ Yu'addu'un means they will be shoved and driven with harshness. "Yawm" (the day) is a substitute (badal) for the time-expression mentioned earlier.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 15:

﴿Is this magic? Or do you not see?﴾ A rebuke to the disbelievers for what they used to say in the world, that the Qur'an is magic. ﴿Or do you not see?﴾ Also a rebuke to them, and a mockery of them, meaning: Do you not see this punishment that has befallen you, just as in the world you did not see the realities?

Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 16:

﴿So be patient, or be not patient; it is all the same for you.﴾ The intention here is not a command to be patient, nor a prohibition against it. Rather, the intention is to equate patience and impatience, in that each of the two states will not benefit them, nor will it lighten any of the punishment for them. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ This is a reason (ta'lil) for the punishment they have been described as receiving, not a reason for patience or for its absence, as some people have said.

﴿Fakihin﴾ may mean "possessors of fruit," so that it is like *laban* and *tamir* (one who has milk and one who has dates). Or it may come from *al-fukaha*, meaning joy and delight.

﴿And He protected them﴾ is coordinated with His words ﴿in gardens﴾, or with ﴿their Lord gave them﴾. Or the *waw* is circumstantial (*hal*).

﴿Eat and drink﴾ means: it will be said to them, "Eat and drink."

﴿Wholesome (*hani'an*)﴾ is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun (*masdar*), whose estimated form is "Eat an eating that is wholesome." It may also have taken the place of a verb, whose estimated form is "May the eating and drinking be wholesome for you."

﴿With wide-eyed houris﴾: *al-hur* is the plural of *hawra'*, one whose white of the eye is very white and whose black is very black. *Al-'in* is the plural of *'ayna'*, one with large eyes together with beauty. The particle *bi* entered on ﴿bi-hurin﴾ because His words ﴿and We married them﴾ include the meaning of "We paired them," as al-Zamakhshari said. He also said that ﴿Those who believed﴾ is coordinated with ﴿bi-hurin 'in﴾, meaning: We paired them with houris for the pleasure of them, and with those who believed for companionship with them. The more evident view is that the speech is complete at ﴿with wide-eyed houris﴾, and ﴿those who believed﴾ is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is ﴿We have joined﴾ 'adhab.

﴿And those who believed, and their offspring followed them in faith﴾: the meaning of the verse is what is reported in the noble hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believer to his rank in Paradise, even if they fall short of him in deeds, so that his eye may be comforted by them." This is an honor for the children because of their fathers. It was said that this refers to the children who died in childhood. It was also said that it is general, applying to all believing children. *Bi-iman* (with faith) is in the position of a circumstantial phrase (*hal*) relating to the offspring, and the meaning is that they followed their fathers in faith. Al-Zamakhshari said that this prepositional phrase is connected to ﴿We have joined﴾, so that the meaning, in his view, is that by means of faith We joined their offspring to them. The first view is more evident.

If it is asked, "Why did He say *bi-iman* (with faith) in the indefinite form?" the answer is: the meaning is with some faith, by which they were not worthy of their fathers' rank, yet they were joined to them as an honor to the fathers. So the intent is the minimal faith of the offspring, and yet their rank was raised. How much more so when their faith is great.

﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾: that is, We did not reduce for them any of the reward of their deeds, but rather We fully repaid them their wages. It was also said that the meaning is: We joined their offspring to them, and We did not reduce anything of the reward of their deeds because of that; rather, We did this as an added favor beyond the reward of their deeds. The pronoun, according to both views, refers to those who believed. It was also said that it refers to the offspring.

﴿Every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾: that is, held in pledge. Either his good deeds will save him, or his evil deeds will destroy him.

The pronoun, according to both views, refers to those who believed. It was also said that it refers to the offspring.

﴿Every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾: that is, held in pledge. Either his good deeds will save him, or his evil deeds will destroy him.

﴿Fakihin﴾ may mean "possessors of fruit," so that it is like *laban* and *tamir* (one who has milk and one who has dates). Or it may come from *al-fukaha*, meaning joy and delight.

﴿And He protected them﴾ is coordinated with His words ﴿in gardens﴾, or with ﴿their Lord gave them﴾. Or the *waw* is circumstantial (*hal*).

﴿Eat and drink﴾ means: it will be said to them, "Eat and drink."

﴿Wholesome (*hani'an*)﴾ is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun (*masdar*), whose estimated form is "Eat an eating that is wholesome." It may also have taken the place of a verb, whose estimated form is "May the eating and drinking be wholesome for you."

﴿With wide-eyed houris﴾: *al-hur* is the plural of *hawra'*, one whose white of the eye is very white and whose black is very black. *Al-'in* is the plural of *'ayna'*, one with large eyes together with beauty. The particle *bi* entered on ﴿bi-hurin﴾ because His words ﴿and We married them﴾ include the meaning of "We paired them," as al-Zamakhshari said. He also said that ﴿Those who believed﴾ is coordinated with ﴿bi-hurin 'in﴾, meaning: We paired them with houris for the pleasure of them, and with those who believed for companionship with them. The more evident view is that the speech is complete at ﴿with wide-eyed houris﴾, and ﴿those who believed﴾ is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is ﴿We have joined﴾ 'adhab.

﴿And those who believed, and their offspring followed them in faith﴾: the meaning of the verse is what is reported in the noble hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believer to his rank in Paradise, even if they fall short of him in deeds, so that his eye may be comforted by them." This is an honor for the children because of their fathers. It was said that this refers to the children who died in childhood. It was also said that it is general, applying to all believing children. *Bi-iman* (with faith) is in the position of a circumstantial phrase (*hal*) relating to the offspring, and the meaning is that they followed their fathers in faith. Al-Zamakhshari said that this prepositional phrase is connected to ﴿We have joined﴾, so that the meaning, in his view, is that by means of faith We joined their offspring to them. The first view is more evident.

If it is asked, "Why did He say *bi-iman* (with faith) in the indefinite form?" the answer is: the meaning is with some faith, by which they were not worthy of their fathers' rank, yet they were joined to them as an honor to the fathers. So the intent is the minimal faith of the offspring, and yet their rank was raised. How much more so when their faith is great.

﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾: that is, We did not reduce for them any of the reward of their deeds, but rather We fully repaid them their wages. It was also said that the meaning is: We joined their offspring to them, and We did not reduce anything of the reward of their deeds because of that; rather, We did this as an added favor beyond the reward of their deeds. The pronoun, according to both views, refers to those who believed. It was also said that it refers to the offspring.

﴿Every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾: that is, held in pledge. Either his good deeds will save him, or his evil deeds will destroy him.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 22:

﴿And We provided them with fruit﴾. Al-imdad (supplying, providing continuously) is increase repeated again and again.

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 23:

﴿They pass around therein a cup⁠﻿﻿—﻿﻿ meaning, they hand it to one another, as they sit together over the drink﴾ ﴿Therein is no idle talk nor any sinful word﴾. Lagha (idle talk) is worthless speech, and ta'thim is sin, so it is unlike the wine of this world.

"Youths of their own, as if they were hidden pearls" (Qur'an 52:24). "Youths" (ghilman) means their attendants. "As if they were hidden pearls": al-lu'lu' is a gem, and al-maknun is that which is guarded and kept safe, and this is on account of their beauty. It was also said: it is the pearl that has not yet come out of its oyster shell.

They said, "Indeed, we were before this among our people, fearful [of Allah]."
That is, we were in the world fearful of Allah. Ishfaq (مُشْفِقِينَ) is intense fear.

﴿فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ﴾
"So Allah bestowed His favour upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind (al-Samum)."
Al-Samum (ٱلسَّمُومِ) is the most intense heat. It has also been said that it is one of the names of Hell (Jahannam).

﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ﴾
"Indeed, we used to call upon Him before."
This may mean "we used to worship Him," or it may derive from du'a (دعاء) in the sense of turning to Him with desire. By "before," they mean in the world, before meeting Allah.

﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾
"Indeed, He is the Most Good (al-Barr), the Most Merciful."
Al-Barr is the One who shows goodness to His servants and treats them kindly.
Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read inna (أنَّهُ) with a fatha on the hamza, making it a maf'ul li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or making this phrase itself the object of the calling. The rest of the readers read it with a kasra, as a new independent sentence (isti'naf).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 29:

﴿So remind, for by the grace of your Lord you are not a soothsayer (kahin) nor a madman (majnun)﴾. This is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: remind the people. Then He negated from him what the disbelievers attributed to him of soothsaying (kahanah) and madness (junun). And the meaning of ﴿by the grace of your Lord﴾ is: by reason of Allah's favour upon you.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 30–31:

﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ "Am" (أم) in this place and in what follows is interrogative, in the sense of denunciation (al-inkar). Tarabbus (التربص) means waiting, and rayb al-manun (ريب المنون) means the calamities of time (hawadith al-dahr). It was also said that it means death. The Quraysh had said: "He is only a poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time, so that he will perish just as those poets before him perished, such as Zuhayr and al-Nabigha." ﴿Say, "Wait; I am with you among those who wait."﴾ This is a command in the form of a threat.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 30–31:

﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ "Am" (أم) in this place and in what follows is interrogative, in the sense of denunciation (al-inkar). Tarabbus (التربص) means waiting, and rayb al-manun (ريب المنون) means the calamities of time (hawadith al-dahr). It was also said that it means death. The Quraysh had said: "He is only a poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time, so that he will perish just as those poets before him perished, such as Zuhayr and al-Nabigha." ﴿Say, "Wait; I am with you among those who wait."﴾ This is a command in the form of a threat.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 32:

﴿Or do their intellects (aḥlām) command them to this?﴾ Aḥlām means ʿuqūl (intellects, reasons). That is: how do their intellects command them to this? The reference of "this" is either their saying that he is a poet (shāʿir), or what they are upon of disbelief and denial. Attributing the command to the intellects is a metaphor (majāz), like His saying: ﴿Does your prayer command you...?﴾ [Hūd: 87]. ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾ Here "am" (أم) means "bal" (بل, "rather"). It may also be that it means "bal" together with the interrogative hamza, which carries the sense of denial (inkār), as it does in all these passages.

Or do they say, "He has invented it"? That is, he fabricated it on his own accord. The pronoun of the subject refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the object refers to the Qur'an. "Then let them produce a statement like it." This is a rebuttal against them and the establishment of proof over them. The imperative here is for *taʻjīz* (a challenge demonstrating their incapacity).

Or do they say, "He has invented it"? That is, he fabricated it on his own accord. The pronoun of the subject refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the object refers to the Qur'an. "Then let them produce a statement like it." This is a rebuttal against them and the establishment of proof over them. The imperative here is for *taʻjīz* (a challenge demonstrating their incapacity).

[Qur'an 52:35] "Were they created from nothing?" On this there are three opinions. The first is that it means: were they created without a Lord who brought them into being and made them His servants? For this reason they do not worship God. The second: were they created without a father or mother, like inanimate objects, so that they are not commanded or forbidden, as is the state of inanimate objects. The third: were they created without being called to account or recompensed for their deeds? On this view it is like His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:115]. ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ means: are they the creators of themselves, such that they do not worship the Creator? Or are they the creators of the created beings, such that they behave arrogantly?

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 37–38:

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ The meaning: Do they have the treasuries of Allah, such that they need not worship Him? It was also said: Do they have the treasuries of Allah, such that they give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish? And that they assign prophethood to whomever they wish?

﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is, the lords who prevail. It was also said: al-Musaytir (the controller) is the one who has authority and dominates.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ That is, do they have a ladder by which they ascend to the heaven and thus hear what the angels say, so that they know the truth of their claim?

Then He silenced them by His saying: ﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority.﴾ That is, a clear proof for their claim.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 40:

﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ Its meaning: Do you ask them for a wage for Islam, so that its payment weighs heavily upon them and following you becomes difficult for them.

Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ The meaning: Do they have knowledge of the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), so that they write down what is in it, until they say: "We will not be resurrected, and even if we are resurrected, we will not be punished"? It was also said: the meaning is: "So that they write down for people sunnahs (customs) and laws (shara'i') of the worship of idols, the releasing of the free-roaming camels (tasyib al-sawa'ib), and the like."

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ This refers to their scheming against the Prophet ﷺ in the Dar al-Nadwa (the council house of the Quraysh), where they consulted together about killing him or expelling him. ﴿Then it is those who disbelieve who will be the ones ensnared﴾, meaning they are the ones defeated in the plot. "Those who disbelieve" refers to those whose discussion has preceded, namely the disbelievers of Quraysh, and the outward noun has been placed in the position of the pronoun. It is also possible that it means all the disbelievers.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 43:

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ The meaning: Do they have a god other than Allah who can protect them from the punishment of Allah and prevent it from them? In this verse Allah confines to a single negation all the meanings that would necessitate arrogance and distance from entering Islam, and He denies them of these, to make clear that their arrogance has no justification and their disbelief has no proof.

Surah 52, verse 44:

﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾

They had asked that a piece of the sky be sent down upon them. The meaning is that even if they were to see a piece of the sky falling upon them, their insolence, ignorance and obstinacy would drive them to say: "It is not a piece (kisf), but rather layered clouds (saḥāb markūm)," meaning: dense, one piled upon another.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 45:

﴿So leave them﴾ is abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e. subject to *naskh*, abrogation) by the sword, ﴿until their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾. It means the Day of Resurrection. The striking therein is the first blast (of the Trumpet). It has been said otherwise, but the correct view is what we have mentioned, because of His saying in al-Ma'arij [44] about the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 47:

﴿That, but most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿A punishment short of that.﴾ He means their being killed on the Day of Badr. It is also said that it is hunger through famine, and it is said: the punishment of the grave.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 52, verse 48:

﴿And be patient for the judgement of your Lord﴾: that is, be patient with their denial of you and with Our granting them respite, for indeed We see you. ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise when you arise﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to saying "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah). The meaning of ﴿when you arise﴾ is from every gathering, and it has been said: he meant "when you arise and when you sit, and in every state," and he took rising as an example. The second is that it refers to the voluntary prayers (nawafil). The third is that it refers to the obligatory prayers (fara'id): so "when you arise" is the Zuhr and the 'Asr, that is, when you rise from the midday nap (qayla); and "and from the night" is the Maghrib and the 'Isha'; and "and the receding of the stars" is the Subh (Fajr). And whoever said that it refers to the voluntary prayers made "the receding of the stars" to be the two rak'ahs of Fajr.
